title: Strict quotient reduction model and completion-unit normalization
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring, $I\subset A$ an ideal, $A_n=A/I^n$ for $n\ge1$, and $T$ a site small in the module universe [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Write $D_T=D(\operatorname{Mod}(\underline A_T))$ for the ordinary unbounded module derived category [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Use the completion reflector $C_T$ with unit $\eta_T$ onto the full derived-complete subcategory of [lem-sp-completed-pullback-adjunction]; thus $C_TV=R\lim_n(V\otimes_A^L\underline{A_n}_T)$. Put $J=\mathbf N_{\ge1}^{\mathrm{op}}$ and use the small diagram site of [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-site-realization]. Its constant ring sheaf is $\Delta\underline A_T$ and its quotient ring sheaf is $B_T=(\underline{A_n}_T)_n$ with the actual quotient transitions. A $B_T$-module system consists of module sheaves $M_n$ over $\underline{A_n}_T$ and $\underline{A_{n+1}}_T$-linear transition maps to $M_n$ by restriction of scalars. Write $\Delta$ for the constant-tower functor, $U_T$ for restriction to constant-$A$ towers, $S_T=-\otimes^L_{\Delta\underline A_T}B_T$, $\mathcal R_T=S_T\Delta$, $i_V:\Delta V\to U_T\mathcal R_TV$ for the quotient augmentation, and $\mathcal L_T=R\lim$ on constant-$A$ towers, with its canonical identification $\ell_V:\mathcal L_T\Delta V\xrightarrow{\sim}V$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. Then: (1) the ring sheaf $B_T$ realizes the category of strict semilinear quotient systems, with componentwise kernels, cokernels and cohomology, and $U_T$ is exact and conservative on derived categories; (2) for every $V\in D_T$, a single flat-term K-flat representative $Q\to V$ [def-pc-kflat-complex, lem-pc-kflat-resolution] gives a K-flat diagonal $\Delta Q$ and represents $\mathcal R_TV$ by the strict complex $(Q\otimes_A\underline{A_n}_T)_n$ with quotient transitions, and under this identification $i_V$ is represented by the termwise quotient maps; (3) the constant-tower functor $\Delta$ preserves K-injective complexes [def-pur-kinjective-complex], and on a K-injective $V$ the map $\ell_V$ is represented by the literal equality $\lim\Delta V=V$; (4) $\mathcal L_TU_T\mathcal R_T=C_T$ canonically, and $\mathcal L_T(i_V)\ell_V^{-1}=\eta_{T,V}$. These are identities of natural transformations in $V$.
